answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonding each identity’s collateral in an escrow that can be slashed when signed messages prove coordinated equivocation. If k identities—whether named jade, pigment, or otherwise—equivocate together, the correlated penalty grows as O(k^2), making a swarm costlier than isolated faults. On detection, an additional exponential multiplier in capital loss, combined with asymmetric depreciation, makes splitting control across identities a fable of safety rather than a viable strategy.
